message: Some customers have seen small card charges they do not recognize. The charges are real and our security team is investigating with our card processor; we do not yet know the cause or how many accounts are affected, and we will tell you as soon as we do. Starting today: if you dispute a card charge, we credit up to $100 right away while we investigate, for the next 8 weeks. You can turn on an alert for every card payment and order a free new card in the app.
why:
The unrecognized charges and the 'Cobalt got hacked' post hit trust three weeks before the migration.
Instant dispute credit and payment alerts give every customer a concrete way to protect themselves today.
Saying what we know and do not know keeps us inside the no-misleading red line.

actions.action: Higher offline card limit during the migration

message: On Sat Dec 12, 00:00 to Sun Dec 13, 12:00 CT, Cobalt moves to a new core banking system. For those 36 hours the app is read-only: you can see your balance, but transfers, P2P payments and new cards are paused. Your card keeps working offline: we raised the limit to $250 per payment for that weekend, and we added support staff for the coming weeks. If something goes wrong the switch can take some hours longer; we will post updates in the app.
why:
Tell customers early and plainly what the migration weekend means.
The $250 offline limit covers most weekend card spending while transfers are paused.
Extra staff keeps support waits short after the charges scare and around the switch.
